Subject: Post-call: MedLytics technical qualification + quant tradeoffs

Hi Olivia / Rajiv — thanks for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discussion so we have a shared plan.

Call summary (high level)
- Primary use case: clinical notes summarization + structured extraction for downstream analytics. Throughput expectation: ~1200 requests/min (avg 1k tokens/request) with 99th p95 latency target ~350ms.
- Data sensitivity: PHI in notes; MedLytics will need VPC/private deployment and audit logs for SOC2 evidence.
- Success criteria: extraction F1 >= 0.88 on our shared eval set; average infer cost below $0.02/request (target).

Model recommendations (initial)
- Candidate A: Mistral-Instruct-7B (FP16/FP8) — strong quality on instruction tasks, good latency on 1-2 GPU groups.
- Candidate B: Llama-2-13B-CHAT quantized with AWQ — favorable throughput and lower memory footprint; watch for edge-case hallucination on rare entity formats.
- Candidate C: Falcon-40B-Compact (GPTQ) — best quality for extraction but higher cost; consider for critical-path weighting.

Quantization note from call: you asked about AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 tradeoffs. We committed to a short write-up and a benchmark pack — attached bench PDF plus the prompt set we used. Basic tradeoff summary: AWQ offers the largest memory savings with small quality regressions for many instruction tasks; GPTQ preserves more float fidelity but is slower at some kernels; FP8 (on supported hardware) gives excellent perf for decoder-only flows but requires validation on extraction metrics.

Immediate next steps
1) We'll upload a Drive folder with: prompt sets, benchmark scripts, and our smaller eval harness (link below).
2) Redwood will run a 48-hour throughput/latency sweep on AWQ and GPTQ variants and share per-prompt F1/EM and latency/cost breakdown. (Ben & Monica to own)
3) MedLytics to confirm a safe subset of notes (anonymized or synthetic) for the pilot and confirm deployment preference (VPC or Private).
4) Schedule pilot kickoff (15–30m) next week to align canary criteria and rollback thresholds.

Attachments: medlytics-promptset-v1.csv (prompt examples and expected labels), rw-inference-latency-cost-bench-202706.pdf (high-level bench and cost model)

Hi Olivia — quick technical follow-up and proposed pilot plan. Marking the items Marissa outlined as owned.

Short answers first:
- Prompt sensitivity: extraction prompts that rely on preserving entity formatting (dates, medication codes, punctuation-delimited lists) tend to be the most sensitive. For example, prompts in row 7–12 of the CSV ("Extract medication list, preserve dosage/unit and TOCC codes") historically show larger delta when moving to very aggressive 3-bit AWQ versus 8-bit GPTQ.
- FP8 availability: FP8 inference paths are available on our private deployment stack only on GPUs that expose the new tensor cores (we can run this in your VPC if you allow those instances). On hosted, FP8 is available in select regions/hardware and requires a compatibility check.

AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 — concise trade summary:
- AWQ (3/4-bit)
  - Pros: huge memory reduction; allows larger batch sizes and higher sustained throughput; lower cost per token.
  - Cons: can introduce token-level perturbations that disproportionately affect extraction labels (entity boundaries), especially with non-standard punctuation.
- GPTQ (4/8-bit variants)
  - Pros: generally preserves logits more faithfully than the most aggressive AWQ; better overall extraction F1 at a moderate memory hit.
  - Cons: slower kernel implementations on some backends; higher memory than AWQ so fewer concurrent contexts.
- FP8 (hardware-accelerated)
  - Pros: closest to FP16 quality in many tests; excellent throughput when supported by hardware; relatively low latency.
  - Cons: limited hardware availability, ops complexity to certify on a private VPC, and dependency on vendor drivers.

Proposed pilot (48–72h sweep)
1) Bench: run AWQ (3-bit), GPTQ-4 and FP8 variants across the promptset with your anonymized sample. Collect per-prompt F1/EM, latency (p50/p95), and cost per 1M tokens.
2) Canary: pick 10 representative extraction prompts (we suggest row 4,7,9,12,15 from the CSV) to be used as canary checks for rollback.
3) Autoscale config: we’ll ship an autoscale policy that respects VPC egress caps and sets conservative ramp steps for evening bursts.
4) Rollout policy: start with a 10% traffic canary on AWQ for 24h, evaluate quality regressions, then expand or fallback to GPTQ/FP8 for the failing prompts via per-route model routing.

Deliverables and owners:
- Bench results + per-prompt delta (Ben) — expected within 48h after we get the anonymized sample.
- Pilot config (Monica) — includes instance sizes (FP8-eligible), autoscale rules, and SLA windows.
- Security checklist (Marissa) — VPC, KMS, SOC2 artifacts.
